entry.title: GS-2 Transition Planning — corrected finding
entry.summary: HKMA issued GS-2 V.1 on 22 September 2026 as a non-statutory SPM guidance note applicable to all authorized institutions. It sets supervisory expectations for governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets, stakeholder engagement, scenario analysis and communication. AIs should have transition-planning documentation in place by 1 July 2030, take active implementation steps beforehand, and be prepared to demonstrate progress 24 months after issuance.

entry.title: Roadmap for Implementing the Hong Kong Investor Identification Regime for the Exchange-traded Derivatives Market
entry.summary: The SFC roadmap schedules HKIDR-DM implementation for Q2 2028, subject to market readiness, testing and rehearsals, and sets preparation milestones for relevant licensed corporations and registered institutions. The proposed Code provision remains to be gazetted and will take effect on a future SFC-determined date.

entry.title: Obtaining client consent under the Hong Kong Investor Identification Regime for the exchange-traded derivatives market (HKIDR-DM)
entry.summary: The SFC says relevant intermediaries will need express consent from individual clients for specified CID and BCAN collection and transfer under HKIDR-DM. It sets out identity-authentication, record and log expectations, while the proposed Code provision remains to be gazetted and its effective date is to be determined by the SFC.

entry.title: Participating banks in IP Financing Sandbox complete credit approval for first batch of pilot cases
entry.summary: HKMA reports that three participating banks completed credit approvals for seven IP Financing Sandbox pilot cases, using independent IP valuation reports in credit assessment. HKMA describes the Sandbox as a risk-controlled pilot and does not state a broader participation requirement or a new supervisory deadline.

entry.title: HSBC names stablecoin ‘HSBC Redcoin’
entry.summary: HSBC announced the name of its planned Hong Kong-dollar stablecoin and says it plans a phased H2 2026 launch, initially through PayMe and the HSBC HK Mobile App for P2P and P2M payments. The bank statement does not confirm a launch date, licence terms, corporate availability, redemption design or cross-border scope.

entry.title: Banking industry further extends loan repayment grace period for affected individuals of Tai Po Fire
entry.summary: HKMA and HKAB announced that all 28 retail banks will extend by a further six months, to end-May 2027, the principal-and-interest repayment grace period for affected individuals’ existing mortgages, personal loans and credit-card loans. Wang Fuk Court mortgagee banks will continue flexible mortgage handling, including extending the original-mortgage grace period until a newly purchased unit is ready for intake.

entry.title: SFC and AFRC extend regulatory cooperation to financial reporting of licensed firms and funds under new MoU
entry.summary: The SFC and AFRC signed a new MoU on 28 September 2026, replacing their February 2021 MoU. It covers financial and, where applicable, compliance reporting by licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers, SFC-authorised funds and registered open-ended fund companies, and related audit and assurance work. The MoU provides for information sharing, referrals, mutual assistance and coordinated inspections or investigations in matters of mutual regulatory interest, subject to law.

entry.title: DBS Hong Kong’s Gen AI-enabled virtual assistants reach over 1 million customers and go agentic
entry.summary: DBS Hong Kong says it will progressively introduce agentic capabilities for DBS IDEAL corporate and SME users from 26 September 2026. DBS says authenticated customers can complete supported banking tasks through conversation; the announcement does not state the underlying control design.

entry.title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Bank Indonesia Strengthen Cooperation in Cross-Border Payments
entry.summary: HKMA and Bank Indonesia signed an MoU to explore QR-code cross-border payment interoperability and hold technical, operational and regulatory dialogues. The announcement states no implementation arrangement, participant requirement or deadline.

entry.title: Review of the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners
entry.summary: HKMA proposes a revised Enhanced Competency Framework for all AIs, including a common Core Level, ten Professional-Level workstreams, revised experience requirements and integrated qualifications. It advises uninterrupted current ECF training while guidance and transition arrangements are developed; milestones are indicative rather than a fixed compliance date.

entry.title: SFC unveils Strategic Action Plan to support Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan and Policy Address in promoting capital market development
entry.summary: The SFC Strategic Action Plan sets out market-development initiatives across RMB internationalisation, mutual access, wealth management, market quality and financial security. The announcement signals initiatives and future consultation, including planned 2027 measures, rather than a binding rule or immediate all-AI obligation.

entry.title: Firms crack down on money mules but need to do more
entry.summary: The FCA reports a completed review of 35 UK retail banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions. It reports suspected mule-account closures and multi-account cash-out patterns, and says it is working with industry and law enforcement on intelligence sharing; this is a UK benchmark, not a Hong Kong requirement.

entry.title: GS-2 Transition Planning
entry.summary: HKMA’s Banking Regulatory Document Repository lists GS-2 Transition Planning as a current circular issued on 22 September 2026 under Green & Sustainable Banking — Climate risk management for all Authorized Institutions. The retained record does not establish its operative expectations, effective date or transition timetable.

entry.title: The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — International Financial Centre
entry.summary: The Policy Address says the HKMA will introduce a seven-day offshore RMB liquidity tender mechanism, explore offshore RMB short-term debt instruments, and encourage more foreign banks in Hong Kong to join CIPS directly. It is market-development direction, not a stated binding requirement or timetable for authorised institutions.

entry.title: Crypto firms get guidance on how the new regime applies
entry.summary: The FCA says its future UK cryptoasset-regime guidance explains which activities may require authorisation, including qualifying-stablecoin issuance, platform operation, dealing or arranging, safeguarding and arranging staking. Applications open on 30 September 2026 and the regime is due to enter force on 25 October 2027; this is a UK benchmark, not a Hong Kong requirement.

entry.title: Policy Address signals future consultation on AI-enabled fraudulent content
entry.summary: The Hong Kong Government says the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau will consult later in 2026 on expanding a legal framework to encourage technology and telecommunications sectors to improve detection and removal of potentially fraudulent online content, including AI-generated content. The announcement states no consultation date, final scope, implementation date or bank duty.

entry.title: SFC circular on Haiti and Yemen sanctions amendments
entry.summary: The SFC reported that the Haiti and Yemen sanctions amendment regulations were gazetted on 11 September 2026 with immediate effect. The underlying regulations are required within their legal scope; the circular addresses licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual-asset service providers and associated entities and does not state a new obligation for authorised institutions generally.

entry.title: Circular on Private Market Investments
entry.summary: HKMA published a current circular on private market investments for Registered Institutions, classified under securities/investment products; registered evidence does not expose its operative text.

entry.title: Consultation on Phase 2B prototype of Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
entry.summary: HKMA opened a Phase 2B Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance consultation for all authorised institutions; comments close on 7 October 2026.

entry.title: Second Reading of the Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Bill – Wrap-Up Speech
entry.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs described proposed scam-countermeasure orders and said local banks will offer an LPBA or alternative basic account from October 2026, with no exact date stated.
